scenarios.name: agent_encoded_powershell
scenarios.description: The Intune management agent runs a device compliance check as SYSTEM: an encoded, policy-bypassing PowerShell command that reads the BitLocker status of C: and writes it to the agent's cache folder.
scenarios.alert: Alert on WIN11-OPS: process powershell.exe. Review this process and its related activity.
scenarios.label_note: Looks like T1059.001 and T1027: a hidden-from-view encoded command run as SYSTEM. The parent is the management agent, the command decodes to a read-only status query, and nothing leaves the host from it.

scenarios.name: procdump_own_service
scenarios.description: A developer takes a full memory dump of their own hung OrderService.exe with Sysinternals ProcDump and writes it to D:\Dumps.
scenarios.alert: Alert on WIN11-OPS: process procdump64.exe. Review this process and its related activity.
scenarios.label_note: Looks like T1003.001: ProcDump opening a process with full access and writing a .dmp. The process dumped is the developer's own service, not lsass.exe.

scenarios.name: scheduled_system_backup
scenarios.description: Task Scheduler starts the nightly Windows Server Backup job: wbadmin start backup takes a shadow copy of C: and the backup engine writes the image to E:\WindowsImageBackup.
scenarios.alert: Alert on WIN11-OPS: process wbadmin.exe. Review this process and its related activity.
scenarios.label_note: Looks like T1490 or T1003.003: wbadmin and the Volume Shadow Copy service. The job creates a backup; nothing is deleted and no hive or ntds.dit is copied out.

scenarios.name: onedrive_first_setup
scenarios.description: At a user's first logon the OneDrive installer that ships with Windows downloads the client, adds its Run key so it starts at logon, and registers its update task.
scenarios.alert: Alert on WIN11-OPS: process OneDriveSetup.exe. Review this process and its related activity.
scenarios.label_note: Looks like T1547.001, T1053.005 and T1105: a download, a Run key and a scheduled task in a few seconds. All three are the stock installer's documented behaviour, from its own path to Microsoft's servers.

scenarios.name: certutil_hash_check
scenarios.description: From an interactive PowerShell window a user runs certutil -hashfile to print the SHA-256 of an installer in their Downloads folder.
scenarios.alert: Alert on WIN11-OPS: process certutil.exe. Review this process and its related activity.
scenarios.label_note: Looks like T1140 or T1105, which certutil is known for. -hashfile only reads a file and prints its hash; nothing is decoded, downloaded or written.

scenarios.name: scheduled_log_archive
scenarios.description: A scheduled task runs a maintenance script as a service account: it zips last month's IIS logs and robocopy moves the archive to a hidden share on the file server.
scenarios.alert: Alert on WIN11-OPS: process powershell.exe. Review this process and its related activity.
scenarios.label_note: Looks like T1560.001 and T1021.002 or T1048: data zipped by a policy-bypassing PowerShell and sent over SMB to a $ share. The data is web server logs, the target is the internal file server, and the task runs from C:\Scripts on a schedule.
